title: Tale of Kamar al-Zaman and Princess Budur
summary: Prince Kamar al-Zaman, son of King Shahriman of the Khaledan Isles, was a youth of such blinding beauty that his name meant 'Moon of the Age.' Yet he was so devoted to scholarsh...
full_text:
Prince Kamar al-Zaman, son of King Shahriman of the Khaledan Isles, was a youth of such blinding beauty that his name meant 'Moon of the Age.' Yet he was so devoted to scholarship, archery, and jurisprudence that he refused his father’s commands to marry, desiring only to rule with wisdom. In anger, his father confined him to an ancient tower.

At that same hour, in the distant empire of China, Princess Budur, whose beauty was famed across the eastern seas, likewise refused all royal suitors, preferring to study astronomy and statecraft, and was placed in a pavilion by her father.

During the night, a benevolent jinni named Danhash and an angelic peri named Maymunah met above the clouds. Arguing over which mortal youth was the fairer in all the world, they lifted Princess Budur from China and placed her gently upon the couch beside Kamar al-Zaman in his tower.

When the prince awakened, he was dazzled by the sleeping maiden’s radiance. Believing his father had placed his bride beside him, he slipped his own royal talismanic ring onto her finger, took her ring in exchange, and kissed her brow before sleep overcame him. When the spirits carried Budur back to China, she awoke with Kamar al-Zaman’s ring upon her hand, her heart consumed by love for the prince she had seen in her vision.

Both kingdoms were plunged into confusion as prince and princess searched the world for their mysterious counterpart. Kamar al-Zaman traveled disguised as an astrologer, while Princess Budur, escaping in the robes of a prince, governed the city of the Ebony Isles with supreme justice.

Recognizing the talismanic ring during an astrological assembly, the royal lovers were joyfully reunited. Their fathers set aside their anger, celebrating a royal union that joined the empires of the West and the East in perpetual friendship.
moral: Destiny unites noble souls across vast distances through faith, steadfastness, and pure intention.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Tale of Kamar al-Zaman"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
